title: Mundus MAPP: Erasmus Mundus Master's in Public Policy (2027-2029)
organization: Mundus MAPP consortium (Central European University, ISS Erasmus University Rotterdam, IBEI Barcelona, University of York)
overview: Two-year joint master's in public policy studied in two countries. Applicants who meet the 1 December 2026 deadline are considered for financial aid, including the Erasmus Mundus scholarship.
country: Multiple countries (Austria, Netherlands, Spain, United Kingdom)
deadline_text: December 1, 2026, 23:59 Central European Time (CET): application deadline for applicants who wish to be considered for financial aid.
funding_details: Official financial-aid page: 'A limited number of EMJM scholarships are awarded to the highest-ranked applicants for the duration of the programme (24 months)', calculated on 'a monthly unit cost of 1400 EUR/month', a maximum of EUR 33,600; the contribution 'assists students in covering travel, visa, installation and subsistence costs, and any other costs'. 'EMJM scholarship recipients receive a full tuition-fee waiver.'
Health insurance for the duration of the studies is purchased by the consortium for all enrolled students

The EMJM scholarship does NOT cover: the Study Visit (EUR 600-1000, spring term of Year 1), the Winter School (EUR 600-1000, Year 2), and travel and visa costs between home countries and the consortium countries and when moving to the Year 2 university

'Since only a small number of the top candidates will be awarded a scholarship, applicants are strongly encouraged to seek external funding.' One institutional scholarship per study track is a 50% tuition waiver with no stipend
First-round decisions on 14 April 2027 include the EMJM scholarship
participation_fee: No CEU application fee for Mundus MAPP applicants
stipend: EUR 1,400 a month for EMJM recipients (maximum EUR 33,600 over 24 months); it also has to cover travel, visa and installation
eligibility: Bachelor's degree of at least three years from a recognised university
At least class 2.1 / Upper Second and a GPA of at least 3.17 out of 4.0, or equivalent
Country of residence must differ from the countries of the chosen study track
Open to European and third-country nationals
education_requirement: Three-year bachelor's degree with Upper Second / GPA 3.17 out of 4.0 or equivalent
application_process: Fill in the online application form linked from the How to apply page
Upload the supporting documents listed by the consortium

sources.label: Financial aid (EMJM scholarship amount, what it does not cover, institutional scholarship)

eligibility_reason: Nationality and degree level fit. The programme requires an Upper Second or a GPA of 3.17 out of 4.0, and the profile does not record the degree grade or an English test score.
potential_issues: Only a limited number of top-ranked applicants receive the EMJM scholarship; the page says to seek external funding as well
The scholarship does not cover travel and visa costs to the consortium countries, nor the Study Visit and Winter School (EUR 600-1000 each)
Degree grade must reach the Upper Second / 3.17 threshold
English-language proof is normally required; no test score is recorded
The consortium urges applicants from visa-sensitive countries to use the first deadline
relevance_reason: Public policy is the closest academic match to the public-sector and policy analyst track, and the Ministry research internship is directly relevant evidence.
action: Convert your degree average to a 4.0 scale. If it reaches 3.17, prepare the application and references before 1 December 2026, tick the interest in a scholarship in the online portal, and budget for travel, visa, the study visit and the winter school, which the scholarship does not pay.
notes: 2 November 2026 (rerun): the financial-aid page was read; the earlier label Fully Funded was not supported (limited awards, EUR 1,400 a month, travel and visa costs not covered), so it is now Substantially Funded.

title: GLOCAL: Erasmus Mundus Master in Global Markets, Local Creativities (2027-2029)
organization: GLOCAL consortium of seven universities (coordinated from the UK)
overview: Two-year international master's on the history, theory and institutions of global capitalism and international business. Erasmus Mundus scholarship applications for the 2027-2029 intake are open.
funding_details: Official scholarship page: 'The Erasmus Mundus Scholarship includes: Full coverage of tuition fees, including deposit'; 'Full insurance coverage'; 'An optional contribution to student travel and installation costs'; 'A monthly subsistence allowance for the entire duration'
Option One: three advances of EUR 1,000 (August, May, September) for visa, travel and installation, then EUR 1,275 a month; Option Two: EUR 1,400 a month without the advances
'No more than 6 scholarships per nationality' over four editions; up to 20 extra scholarships target certain regions (Regions 1, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11); results in April 2027
The pages do not use the words 'fully funded'
stipend: EUR 1,400 a month (Option Two) or EUR 1,275 a month after three advances of EUR 1,000 (Option One)
eligibility: UK 2:1 Honours degree, or the country-specific GPA equivalent
Minimum English-language proficiency for applicants whose first language is not English
nationality_requirements: Scholarships can be offered to students from any region of the world
education_requirement: Bachelor's degree equivalent to a UK 2:1
language_requirement: English proficiency at the level set by the university
application_process: Follow the How To Apply page of the consortium
Submit the scholarship application before 14 January 2027, 13:00 UK time
eligibility_reason: A business administration degree fits the subject. Eligibility depends on the degree grade (UK 2:1 equivalent) and on proof of English, neither of which is recorded in the profile.
potential_issues: A conditional or unconditional University of Glasgow offer is needed before the scholarship application; offers 'holding for documents' at the deadline are not considered

The Glasgow country-specific GPA page (gla.ac.uk/international/country) has no entry for the DRC, so the grade equivalence for a Congolese Licence must be asked of Glasgow (UK entry rule: 2:1 Honours)
English proof is needed by the scholarship deadline
Cap of 6 scholarships per nationality over four editions
Earlier cycles saw inconsistent deadline wording on the entry-requirements page; on 2 November 2026 the scholarship, how-to-apply and entry-requirements pages all gave 14 January 2027, 13:00 UK time
relevance_reason: The curriculum (international business and the global economy) continues a business administration degree directly, and no work experience is required.

visa.support: The travel and installation contribution is intended to help with visa and residence-permit costs.

action: Check the country-specific GPA requirement for DRC degrees on the GLOCAL site, then plan an English test if needed.
notes: Deadline wording preserved from the official home page. Re-read on 29 October 2026: scholarship applications close 14 January 2027, 13:00 UK time; self-funded tracks have other dates. 2 November 2026 (rerun): scholarship, how-to-apply and entry-requirements pages re-read (deadline 14 January 2027, 1300 UK time, consistent). Label lowered from Fully Funded to Substantially Funded: the pages never say fully funded and travel is only an 'optional contribution'. Stays PARTIALLY VERIFIED because the DRC grade equivalence is not published.

title: DAAD In-Country/In-Region scholarships in Sub-Saharan Africa (2027 start)
overview: DAAD scholarships for Sub-Saharan Africans to do a master's or PhD at selected African universities, in the home country or elsewhere in the region. The open calls in the September 2026 overview are all in science, engineering, agriculture, health or education.
country: Multiple countries (Burkina Faso, Ghana, Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, Tanzania, Uganda, Malawi)
program_dates: Start of study between August and November 2027, depending on the programme
deadline_text: Deadlines are set per programme. DAAD's 'Overview Open Calls' (edition 09/2026) lists the programmes; one secondary source gives 12 November 2026 as the application deadline.
funding_details: DAAD programme page: the scholarship 'usually includes': tuition fees; a monthly scholarship rate; a study and research allowance; a printing allowance for the final thesis; and, for In-Region scholars only, a travel allowance and usually funding for health insurance
'Further funding options may be available, depending on the location'; the monthly amount is not on the page
The page does not use the words 'fully funded'
eligibility: Sub-Saharan African citizens with a bachelor's degree (for a master's) or a master's degree (for a PhD)
Admission requirements of the chosen programme and host university
other_requirements: Programmes in the 09/2026 overview: Water and Environmental Engineering (2iE, Burkina Faso); Molecular Cell Biology of Infectious Diseases and Seed Science and Technology (University of Ghana); Agricultural Economics (UDS, Ghana); Environmental Health (Jimma, Ethiopia); Plant Breeding (Chuka, Kenya); Education in Research (Moi, Kenya); Electrical Power Systems (Rwanda); Geomatics (Ardhi, Tanzania); Climate Change and Disaster Management (Busitema, Uganda); Aquaculture and Fisheries Science and Irrigation Engineering (LUANAR, Malawi); Environmental Health (MUBAS, Malawi)
application_process: Read the call for the chosen programme in the DAAD scholarship database
Apply to the host institution and to DAAD as the call describes

sources.label: Secondary summary with the 12 November date

eligibility_reason: The nationality and degree level fit, but none of the 13 programmes on offer is in business or management. The nearest are Agricultural Economics (Ghana) and Climate Change and Disaster Management (Uganda), and their entry requirements were not checked.
potential_issues: No business, management or policy programme in the current overview
Deadline per programme; the 12 November date is from a secondary source
relevance_reason: Well funded and open to DRC citizens, but the subjects on offer are far from the business administration background.
action: Skip unless agricultural economics or disaster management genuinely fits your plans.
notes: 2 November 2026 (rerun): programme page and the 09/2026 open-calls overview PDF re-read; label lowered from Fully Funded to Substantially Funded because the official wording is itemised ('usually includes'), not 'fully funded'. The 12 November date still comes only from a secondary source; the overview lists programmes and start months but no deadlines.

title: FAO Internship Programme for Africa (RAF), Call for Expression of Interest 2601980
organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), Regional Office for Africa (RAF)
overview: Call for expressions of interest for FAO internships under the Regional Office for Africa. Interns are assigned to fields matching their profile and the Organization's needs and perform the tasks in Terms of Reference prepared by the hiring office. FAO pays a monthly stipend to interns not sponsored by a university or other entity.
program_dates: Assignments of 3 to 11 months according to the aggregator; the duration field was not readable on the official page.
deadline_text: Posting 21/Sep/2026; closing 31/Dec/2026, 11:59:00 PM (FAO recruitment portal, displayed in Europe/Rome time).
funding_details: 'FAO provides a monthly stipend to interns if they are not sponsored by sending universities or other entities.' The amount is not stated
'FAO does not charge any fee at any stage of the recruitment process'
Travel, accommodation, visa and insurance are not mentioned on the vacancy
participation_fee: None: FAO does not charge any fee at any stage of the recruitment process
stipend: Monthly stipend for interns not sponsored by a university or other entity; amount not stated
eligibility: Enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate degree programme at a bona fide institution at the time of application, or a recent graduate (qualifications must be from a WHED-listed institution)
Specialise in a field relevant to the mission and work of FAO
Working knowledge of at least one FAO language (Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian or Spanish); a second is an asset
Able to adapt to an international multicultural environment, good communication skills
Not previously an FAO intern; no mother, father, sister or brother employed by FAO
Appropriate residence or immigration status in the proposed country of assignment before joining
nationality_requirements: National of an FAO Member (the Democratic Republic of the Congo has been an FAO Member since 9 November 1961)
Candidates from LIFDCs, LDCs, LLDCs and SIDS are encouraged to apply
education_requirement: Currently enrolled (undergraduate or graduate) or recent graduate, from a WHED-listed institution; 'recent' is not defined on the vacancy
language_requirement: Working knowledge of at least one FAO language (French and English both qualify)
other_requirements: Field of study relevant to FAO's work
documents_required: Evidence of attendance at a recognised university or copy of academic qualifications
Complete online profile with employment records, qualifications and language skills
application_process: Create and complete a profile on Jobs at FAO
Attach the motivation letter and academic documents
Apply to vacancy 2601980 before 31 December 2026; only qualified applicants are contacted for interviews
Unsuccessful candidates must re-apply to new calls to stay in consideration

sources.label: FAO vacancy 2601980: Call for Expression of Interest - Internship Programme for Africa (RAF)

eligibility_reason: Nationality (FAO Member), languages and the upper age limit are met. Whether a Licence obtained in 2024 counts as 'recent graduate' is not defined on the vacancy, and the profile does not record whether the university is in WHED or the exact age against the 21-year minimum.
potential_issues: 'Recent graduate' is not defined; a 2024 graduate may fall outside FAO's usage
Stipend amount not stated; travel and housing not mentioned
Interns need residence or immigration status in the country of assignment before joining
Expression-of-interest pool: applying does not guarantee an assignment

2 November 2026: the vacancy page (job 2601980) returned empty fields ('Job Posting', 'Closure Date' blank) to both readers, so the 31 December 2026 closing date could not be re-read; open it in a browser
benefits: UN work experience in FAO's Africa offices
relevance_reason: A paid UN internship in Africa suits operations, programme coordination and policy interests, and French is an FAO language. The open questions are the 'recent graduate' condition and how the stipend compares with living costs.

visa.required: Depends on the country of assignment

upfront_cost_risk: Medium: travel to the duty station is not mentioned as paid
action: Check that your university is listed in WHED (whed.net), then complete a Jobs at FAO profile and apply to vacancy 2601980 with a motivation letter and diploma before 31 December 2026.
notes: The vacancy text was extracted from the FAO Taleo page's embedded data; the portal's hidden time-zone field is Europe/Rome, so 31 Dec 2026 23:59 is taken as CET (22:59 UTC). The aggregator shows '1 January 2027 at 12:59 AM', consistent with a one-hour time-zone shift.
